newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Sundays - April 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Sundays - April 6.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
THE OBSERVER
-- UTILITIES FACE NEW 3BN STG A YEAR TAX THREAT

The Wood Committee, set up by the Department of Environment, is considering a proposal to linking business rates to profits which could cost the privatised utilities more than 3bn stg a year. The privatised utilities are already facing the prospect of a windfall tax if the Labour Party win the general election.
-- MILLIONS LOST IN MORGAN GRENFELL DEALS

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell is thought to have lost millions on high-risk options and futures at its New York office. The investment bank's image has already been tarnished by the Peter Young scandal and the sacking of fund manager Nicola Horlick.
-- LENDERS SET TO RAISE COST OF FIXED LOANS
Mortgage lenders may raise the cost of fixed-rate loans this week after a pre-election rush due to the widely held belief that interest rates will have to rise after the forthcoming general election.
-- 'BLACK FOOTBALLERS ARE LESS WELL PAID,' SAYS STUDY

Dr Stefan Szymanski, senior lecturer at Imperial College Management School, said a representative study of 39 football clubs since 1978 has revealed soccer bosses are discriminating against black players over pay.
- THOMSON BID COULD LEAD TO RADICAL REVAMP AT GEC

A successful Anglo-French bid for the Thomson-CSF electronics company could lead to a radical restructuring of GEC . The deal would mark a major strategic development in the European defence industry.
THE SUNDAY TIMES
-- SOARING GROWTH RAISES PRESSURE FOR RATE RISE

The British economy is growing at a rate of more than 4 percent according to a report to be published this week by Lehman Brothers. The report will put pressure on the government to raise interest rates.
-- BG SET FOR VICTORY OVER REGULATOR

BG, the demerged pipeline arm of British Gas, is likely to win an unexpected battle against industry regulator Ofgas this week. The Monopolies Commission is concerned that large price cuts demanded by Ofgas's Clare Spottiswoode would hit BG shareholders.
-- TORIES INCREASE THEIR LEAD AMONG SMALL BUSINESSES

The Tories have increased their share of the small business vote to 43 percent according to a quarterly small-business survey by Office World. However, a large number of those polled remain uncertain of which party to vote for.
-- INVESTORS PRESS MEPC TO REOPEN MERGER TALKS
The Co-operative Insurance Society, PDFM and Mercury Asset Management are likely to put pressure on property group MEPC's to reopen merger talks with its smaller rival Hammerson.
-- BRITISH ENERGY MOVES INTO GAS

Industry expert believe British Energy and Elf are likely to invest in the 1 bn stg project to build a gas-fired power station on the south Humber, near Hull. The plan is one of the largest independent projects since the industry was privatised.
INDEPENDENT ON SUNDAY
-- PENSIONS SCANDAL CONTINUES

Granada TV's "World In Action" programme will allege tomorrow that mis-selling is still widespread in the industry despite a three-year review to clean it up. Barclays Life, Abbey Life and London & Manchester Assurance are among ten firms criticised in the programme. The Independent on Sunday revealed that Allied Dunbar will also be criticised.
-- SUGAR TRADER HIDES CUBA DEALS
Industry experts believe that commodity group E D & F Man has disguised its involvement in Cuba through a London-based firm, Pacol, to avoid the tough US Helms-Burton Act.
-- NIGERIAN CONMEN MOVE INTO HONG KONG

The Metropolitan Police is warning of bogus Hong Kong firms set up by Nigerians. They are trying to exploit the confusion over the colony's handover to China and con firms out of large amounts of money.
-- CITY JITTERS OVER LABOUR TAX PLANS

Broker Merrill Lynch is worried about that an incoming Labour government might have to raise corporation tax by 2 percent to fund its 1998-99 budget. The City is also worried that Gordon Brown could raise employers' national insurance contributions to pay for Labour's plans.
-- RANK TIPPED FOR TUSSAUDS BID

The City believe Rank could be interested in bidding for the Tussauds Group, a subsidiary of Pearson. Rank said last week it wanted to invest 300m stg a year for the next five years in the leisure industry.
MAIL ON SUNDAY
-- SHAKE-UP IN THE CITY TO COST 20,000 JOBS

US insurance broking group Aon Corporation's expansion plans in London and US could prompt extensive cost cutting in the industry affecting well established names like Alexander Howden, Sedgwick and Minet. Edward Snell, director of recruitment firm IPS Group, said there had already been a number of redundancies.
-- RAIL FRANCHISES 'HEADING FOR THE BUFFERS'

A report commissioned by Save Our Railways will this week reveal that ten privatised rail franchises including Thameslink and three run by Prism are facing financial disaster and may have to be bailed out with taxpayers' money.
-- BOSSES AT SEARS MAY AXE STRONG

Sears Plc chief executive Liam Strong could be dismissed at tomorrow's meeting because of institutional investors concerns at dismal trading figures. The position of chairman Sir Bob Reid, a supporter of Strong, could also be questioned.
-- PAYMENT IN SHARES PLAN FOR DIRECTORS

Glaxo Wellcome is to start paying its non-executive directors after suggestions last month by investment institution Hermes. Booker, Liberty and Unigate may follow suit. However, shareholder action group Pirc have objected saying the move will compromise independence.
-- BILLIONAIRES SET SAIL FOR DOCKLANDS

Singapore businessman Ong Beng Seng and Saudi Prince al Waleed bin Talal are set to invest more than 200mn stg in London's Dockland. They should receive planning consent this week to build a new property development alongside the Thames near Canary Wharf.
SUNDAY EXPRESS
-- COAL GIANT PINS HOPES ON LABOUR

RJB Mining's long-term future could be secured if the Labour Party win the general election. The party is committed to "clean coal" technology as part of its plan for renewable energy sources. RJB had been hit by the recent dash to build cheaper gas-fired power stations.
-- LEICESTER FLOAT FACES EXTRA TIME

Leicester City's plan for a stock market flotation could be held back after strong opposition from at least two shareholders over the proposed share restructuring. There are three classes of shareholders each with different voting rights at present.
-- REED UPS ITS US WAR CHEST
There is growing speculation that Anglo-Dutch publishing group Reed-Elsevier is looking for a major acquisition in the US after substantial raising its credit rating.
-- 'FAT CAT' SLAMS CITY PAY
Former chairman of Northern Electric, David Morris, has criticised the high level of bonuses paid out in the City. He called for a Greenbury or Cadbury style report to tackle the problem.
-- TESCO DOUBLES STAKE IN LUCRATIVE CENTRAL EUROPE

Supermarket group Tesco Plc is to double its capital investment in eastern and central Europe this year. The group will spend 70mn stg in the next 12 months refurbishing and rebanding its stores under the Tesco name.
